messages:
maria: hey, anyone seen weirdness with the Go SDK generator streams + context cancel + auth retries?
kevin: saw something similar yesterday — canceling the ctx doesn't always stop the streaming goroutine for me. still gets a few more tokens out.
oliver: can you paste a short repro? sounds like a race between token refresh and ctx.Done select.
maria: minimal snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
for resp.Next() {
  tok := resp.ReadToken()
  // print token
}
```
when the auth middleware triggers a refresh, the SDK does a retry and we see streaming continue even after cancel.
sara: @maria do you have logs showing the retry/refresh path? maybe the retry is on a separate request goroutine that isn't observing the original ctx.
maria: yup — log shows `auth: refresh token start` then `ctx canceled` then `auth: refresh token finish` and then more tokens.
kevin: hmm — our retry logic wraps the request but the auth refresh uses its own internal context with background to avoid leaking. that was intentional but maybe wrong for streams.
oliver: agreed. For non-streaming calls it's fine, but streaming needs to be cooperative. We should short-circuit refresh if the parent ctx is done.
sara: small workaround for customers: call `cancel()` and then close the resp body (if they have it) — but awkward.
maria: can confirm calling `resp.Close()` stops everything immediately. but that's not ergonomic for generator API since users expect ctx cancel to be enough.
kevin: proposal: change auth refresh to accept a `parentCtx` and do: `select { case <-parentCtx.Done(): return context.Canceled }` before doing background refresh. Also check points where we spawn goroutines during retries.
oliver: also add tests that simulate immediate ctx cancel mid-stream and assert no further tokens emitted.
kevin: filed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/718 (WIP) — touches client/transport/retry.go and auth/refresh.go.
dev-bot: created issue #4312: "go-sdk: generator stream continues after context cancel when auth refresh in-flight" assigned to @kevin.
sara: leaving note: need to check client-side backpressure too — if token emission is buffered, cancel won't drain buffer automatically.
maria: thanks — can we get a patch release? this causes real user confusion in sample apps. customers think cancel doesn't work.
kevin: will push fix to canary today, add changelog entry, and cut a patch if canary looks good tomorrow. :thumbsup:
mar ia: awesome — happy to test sample app and add a small README warning until patch lands.
kevin: great. follow-up tasks: add integration test, update sample app to call `resp.Close()` in cleanup, and add telemetry event when generator is aborted.
